note.note:
History:
- Main complaint: Low energy/fatigue and difficulty getting up, ongoing ~2 months.
- Onset/context: Symptoms began around the time he started a new job (~2 months ago).
- Course/symptoms:
  - Fatigue throughout the day; routine tasks feel harder than usual.
  - Sleep disturbance: Difficulty sleeping; not waking early but trouble sleeping at all.
  - Appetite: Eating less; reduced appetite.
  - Cognitive: Poor concentration, easily distracted.
  - Mood: Lower mood recently; decreased interest/libido over the past few months.
  - Sexual function: Morning erections—initially reported not noticing them recently, later stated no change (conflict noted).
  - Exertional symptoms: Shortness of breath with sports/exertion over the last few months.
- Safety: Denies suicidal or homicidal thoughts.
- Other review: No visual changes.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism.
- Medications: Levothyroxine/“Thyroxine” (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father died by suicide ~15 years ago; otherwise denies family psychiatric conditions. Mother well. Only child.
- Social: Married. Started a new job ~2 months ago. Tobacco/alcohol/substance use not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded.

Impression:
- Subacute fatigue with insomnia, low mood, reduced appetite/libido, and exertional dyspnea for ~2 months temporally associated with a new job; denies SI/HI.
- Plausible diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood: Low mood, insomnia, low energy, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, decreased interest/libido, temporal link to job change.
  - Thyroid dysfunction related to known hypothyroidism/levothyroxine dosing: Fatigue/low mood/low libido could reflect under-replacement; insomnia/dyspnea could reflect over-replacement—labs required.
  - Anemia: Fatigue and new exertional dyspnea warrant CBC/iron studies.
- Note: Conflicting report regarding change in morning erections (see Quality checks).

Management Plan:
- In-person evaluation: Patient to book GP appointment within the next few days for full examination and blood tests (as advised during visit).
- Suggested investigations (to be ordered at in-person visit, guided by history):
  - Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) given hypothyroidism and symptoms.
  - CBC with differential; iron studies (ferritin, iron/TIBC) for anemia evaluation.
  - Consider vitamin B12 and vitamin D levels for fatigue/cognitive/mood symptoms.
  - Consider morning total testosterone if low libido persists after addressing depression/thyroid.
- Mental health assessment:
  - Screen with PHQ-9 (and consider GAD-7) to assess severity and guide management.
  - Discuss counseling/CBT if depressive symptoms are confirmed and impacting function.
- Sleep and lifestyle:
  - Reinforce sleep hygiene (consistent schedule, limit screens/caffeine/alcohol before bed).
  - Gradual return to regular physical activity as tolerated.
- Safety net:
  - Seek urgent care if severe or worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, fainting, or if suicidal thoughts develop.

Patient Summary:
- Middle-aged man with 2 months of fatigue, insomnia, low mood, reduced appetite/libido, and exertional dyspnea starting around a new job. History of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. No SI/HI. Plan is in-person exam and blood tests to evaluate mood disorder, thyroid status, and anemia.

Key Takeaways:
- Book an in-person GP visit within days for exam and targeted blood work.
- Monitor mood, sleep, and breathing; complete standardized mood screening (PHQ-9) at follow-up.
- Seek urgent care for red-flag symptoms (chest pain, severe shortness of breath, fainting, or suicidal thoughts).

Next Steps:
- Schedule GP appointment and labs.
- Review lab results and screening scores in follow-up to finalize diagnosis and treatment plan.
- Consider referral to mental health services if depressive symptoms persist or worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements:
  - Vitals, physical exam findings, weight/BMI, recent weight change.
  - Detailed medication reconciliation (levothyroxine dose, adherence, timing), last thyroid labs.
  - Full ROS (chest pain, palpitations, edema, GI/constipation, heat/cold intolerance, fevers, night sweats).
  - Social history: Tobacco, alcohol, caffeine, recreational drugs, sleep schedule, occupational stressors detail.
- Conflicts:
  - Morning erections: Initially “not noticing them recently,” later “no change” (conflict noted).
  - Symptom duration: Initially “few weeks,” clarified to ~2 months (finalized as ~2 months).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor audio/freeze and brief hypo/hyperthyroid wording confusion, corrected to hypothyroid.
